record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests a new fractal-dimension measure for predicting generalization gaps, using conditional mutual information rather than the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
record.gate_note: Reports competition scores for the proposed measure and a Jacobian Norm comparator. Batch sizes of 64 often failed and those results are omitted from Table 1; this is stated in the text, not a reported result row.
record.test_reason: The study cites the sharpness findings underlying V7 but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare its ranking with other measures. Its own results evaluate fractal-dimension and Jacobian measures, which test none of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose a fractal-dimension measure, judge it uncompetitive with the best techniques, and identify improvements to boundary approximation, dimension estimation, and stability. Large variance is suggested rather than established by repeated-run uncertainty estimates.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces correlation-dimension estimates of model and training-data class boundaries, evaluated by competition conditional mutual information; V7 measures magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size and R percentile range affect the measure; increasing the number of batches did not improve performance. Smaller batches often failed, and higher upper bounds for R percentiles tended to underperform.

fits_no_version.finding: The fractal-dimension measure scores 0.026–0.041 on Task 1 and 0.011–0.020 on Task 2, versus Jacobian scores of 0.0094 and 0.031. Its relative performance differs across tasks and estimation settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A decision-boundary correlation-dimension measure has some predictive association with generalization, with performance dependent on task and estimation settings.

record.problems: The authors state that the measure has large variance and that more experiments are needed. Batch size 64 often failed and those results are omitted. Performance is reported only as competition conditional mutual information; the text gives no uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under random versus natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under different tuning regimes.
Training batch size, fixed epoch budgets, and recipe adaptations. The reported batch sizes concern post-training dimension estimation.
Effects of dropout, dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay on test error.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The text does not identify which dataset corresponds to each task. All row subjects should specify pretrained competition convolutional classifiers; their scores describe measure performance, not individual models' generalization gaps. No supplied result supports a verdict on magnitude-aware sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: Width beyond interpolation and test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
